summary:
**NOVIS (Neural Onboard Vitality & Intelligence System)** is an AI-assisted astronaut health intelligence platform developed to support behavioural and physiological health monitoring during space missions. The prototype integrates facial emotion analysis, personalized baseline calibration, a Psychological Stress Index (PSI), seven-day chronic stress analysis, Burnout Risk Scoring (BRS), recovery assessment and crew health monitoring within a unified mission operations dashboard.

NOVIS addresses the challenges of astronaut isolation, prolonged mission stress and limited access to continuous health assessment by combining behavioural indicators with physiological telemetry. Its interactive telemetry simulator, database persistence and WebSocket-based updates demonstrate real-time data processing and monitoring capabilities.

The project is important because astronaut well-being directly influences cognitive performance, crew coordination and mission readiness. NOVIS aims to move beyond conventional health monitoring towards personalized, proactive astronaut health intelligence, with future scope for wearable sensor integration, predictive AI and validation under simulated spaceflight conditions.
details:
Project Details – NOVIS

NOVIS (Neural Onboard Vitality & Intelligence System) is an AI-assisted astronaut health intelligence platform designed to monitor behavioural well-being, physiological indicators and mission readiness during space missions.

Working Mechanism: NOVIS uses facial emotion analysis through DeepFace and OpenCV to identify behavioural patterns and establish personalized resting baselines through a five-sample calibration process. Its Psychological Stress Index (PSI) combines emotional affect, individual baseline deviation, task complexity and motion-related factors. The platform also incorporates seven-day chronic stress analysis, Burnout Risk Scoring (BRS), recovery assessment and crew-level health monitoring. A telemetry injection simulator demonstrates real-time data processing, database persistence and WebSocket-based dashboard updates.

Benefits and Intended Impact: NOVIS aims to support early identification of accumulating stress, fatigue and reduced recovery patterns. It provides a centralized interface for monitoring individual astronauts and crew health, potentially supporting flight surgeons in evaluating well-being and mission readiness. This is particularly important for long-duration missions, where isolation, confinement and delayed medical assistance present significant challenges.

Technology Used: The system was developed using Python, JavaScript, React, Vite, FastAPI, SQLite, SQLAlchemy, DeepFace and OpenCV. WebSockets enable real-time communication between the backend and dashboard. A webcam supports facial calibration and analysis, while physiological telemetry is currently demonstrated through simulated and externally supplied data. Actual wearable hardware integration remains future work.

Creativity and Design Considerations: The creative aspect of NOVIS lies in combining personalized behavioural analysis, stress scoring, physiological telemetry and crew-level monitoring within a unified aerospace-oriented platform. The design considers individual emotional baselines, data privacy, missing sensor readings, astronaut variability, usability and the need to distinguish experimental behavioural indicators from medical measurements. Its modular architecture allows future integration of wearable sensors, multimodal AI and predictive health analytics.
